PRESS RELEASE: This is a crisis and the Government's response will do nothing for most New Zealanders. The situation demands far more than what was announced today.

🔗 Full press release: 

www.greens.org.nz/government_s...

PRESS RELEASE: Greens Offer Votes To National Party For Immediate Relief In Fossil Fuel Crisis. 

www.greens.org.nz/greens_offer...
Isn't it interesting that protecting rivers is "too costly" but polluting them isn't?
Isn't it interesting that secure housing is called unrealistic, yet tax incentives for landlords aren’t?
Isn’t it interesting that te Tiriti o Waitangi allows the Crown’s existence on this whenua but it’s “too hard” for the Crown to uphold it?
Isn't it interesting that fuel prices soar but the answer to that is families should take a few things out of their boot?
Isn't it interesting that the system we’re told is best leaves the majority at the bottom and puts the rich few at the top?
Isn't it interesting that making decisions for the sake of public good is debatable, but private profits are untouchable?
Isn't it interesting that the people who say a wealth tax on the mega wealthy is a bad idea are usually mega wealthy themselves?
We need real actions that help regular people hurting from these price increases, and a serious plan to reduce our reliance on fossil fuels so the next crisis does not hit families just as hard.

This crisis has also exposed a deeper failure in the Government’s long-term planning.  

They cancelled the Clean Car Discount, weakened the Clean Car Standard, hiked public transport fares & are locking in further exposure to volatile fossil fuel prices with their LNG terminal.

Many people are already struggling with the daily cost of living. Instead of coming with a plan to alleviate hardship, the Finance Minister has nothing on the table to give the support that is needed.

Today, our Finance Minister pulled together a press conference to announce that there is no new support on the way for families, despite it costing $23 more than normal to fill an average petrol car & $36 more to fill a diesel car.
#BREAKING: Nicola Willis tells New Zealanders her plan for fuel prices is: ¯\(ツ)/¯

The Coalition Government love giving the rich more money and aren’t shying away from corporate welfare.

The common factor in cancelling policies like the Clean Car Discount and GIDI fund was that they were reducing emissions (and therefore our exposure to high oil prices.)

If Nicola Willis really didn’t want to hand out lots of money to rich people, why the billions in tax cuts for landlords? 

It’s an absolute rubbish excuse to cancel a policy that was demonstrably working to bring in EVs and low emissions vehicles.

The price of petrol is rising. Meanwhile, the Luxon Government has cancelled the Clean Car Discount and is potentially scrapping the Clean Car Standard, two options which would reduce our need for fuel in the long term.
